findings.description: An increased application has been filed for the retirement community here, seeking an eight-storey complex behind the landmarked three-storey brick building Julia Morgan designed, which was completed in 1925 for the San Francisco Ladies' Protection and Relief Society and designated a San Francisco landmark in 2024 as a Jacobethan Revival building. The two-structure development would span 196,700 square feet, of which 134,180 square feet is housing; the Morgan building would keep ten apartments and the new structure would hold 112 independent-living and eight assisted-living units, over a basement garage for 29 cars and 46 bicycles. The application invokes the State Density Bonus law for a 20% increase over base zoning. Heritage on the Marina and Sequoia Living filed jointly; HKIT Architects is designing the new construction and the alterations, and Page & Turnbull is overseeing historic preservation. An existing cottage would be moved to the corner of Francisco and Laguna and rehabilitated as a Julia Morgan Museum, and the wrought iron perimeter fencing retained. The 1957 Perry Building and the 1963 Health Care Center would be demolished.
